transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14   Time: 15:00 UTC   Duration: 55m
Attendees: Jordan Hale (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (AxiomRetail Head of ML), Marcus Yeo (Backend), Sofia Park (Security)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be partial):
- Purpose: scope POC to characterize workload shape, QPS/concurrency, token distribution, and tail-latency behavior to size Dedicated vs Hosted decision.
- Success criteria discussed: 95th/99th latency SLOs, throughput envelope, cost per 1M tokens, quality regression tolerance.
- Immediate next steps: share traffic logs, Redwood sends benchmark plan and pricing, schedule baseline run.

Topics: workload heatmap, tail latency, cold starts, concurrency, input/output token mix, traffic bursts, data residency, timeline 

-- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, auto-transcribed, speaker labels imperfect) --
00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick rollcall?
00:05 Lena: Hi this is Lena, thanks.
00:07 Marcus: Marcus here.
00:09 Sofia: And Sofia.
00:11 Jordan: Great. Priya and I from Redwood, today's goal is to scope a pilot that will give you a traffic heatmap and tail-latency characterization so you can choose dedicated vs hosted. We'll cover success criteria, benchmarks and timeline.
00:29 Priya: Hi all, I'll be running the technical bits — instrumenting the harness and the KV cache expectations, things like that.
00:39 Lena: Perfect. High level for context — our recommendation engine endpoints see a pretty spiky QPS pattern. Baseline daytime is about 120 QPS but we have bursts to 2.5k for 30-90s. Typical request is a short prompt (40-70 tokens) and a response 120-300 tokens.
01:05 Marcus: The backend is node-based, we use grpc fronting, and we currently call OpenAI for generation. We want to test cost and P99 latency under realistic traffic.
01:20 Priya: Good detail. Can you share tokenization behavior? Are you counting tokens pre or post-truncation?
01:28 Lena: We do pre-truncation, but we also send a few long-context cases for user sessions up to 2,000 tokens occasionally (less than 0.1%).
01:40 Jordan: Noted. For pilot success metrics, what are your SLAs today? P95? P99? 
01:46 Lena: Internally we aim for p95 < 250ms and p99 < 600ms for interactive features. For ranking endpoints p95 < 150 ms, but that's a separate bucket.
02:00 Marcus: The ranking calls are CPU-only and low-latency so not in scope for this POC. This is generation endpoints.
02:07 Priya: Ok the scope then: size based on observed QPS envelope, concurrency at tail bursts, token mix, and measure p95/p99 tail-latency, cold-start penalties, and cost per 1M tokens. We'll also test prefix/KV cache effectiveness.
02:29 Sofia: From compliance — we need to validate KMS integration and audit logs. Also residency: EU for EU users.
02:36 Jordan: We'll include a security checklist and our SOC 2 doc. Priya, to you: what inputs do you need to model the heatmap?
02:44 Priya: Ideally: annotated traffic logs with timestamp, latency, request size (tokens in), response tokens out, and a flag for user-session long context. If you can't share raw logs, anonymized CSV with those columns is fine. Also a quick sample of payloads to verify tokenization.
03:01 Marcus: We can export a 7-day window, strip PII, and S3 link it.
03:06 Lena: We'll aim to have that by Thursday.
03:10 Jordan: Excellent. Let's talk measurement harness. We'll run two phases: baseline replay in Redwood sandbox against the same model you use today, and then a stress/soak with scaled arrival curves to exercise 99th.
03:27 Priya: The baseline gives a realistic heatmap — QPS vs time, token distribution percentiles, and concurrency histogram. The stress run will push bursts to your observed 99th percentile and beyond to see where the degradation modes are.
03:41 Lena: How do you handle caching? Our prompts have a lot of repeated prefix for product meta; we want to understand potential prefix/KV cache savings.
03:51 Priya: We do prefix dedupe and KV cache for sessions pinned to same model shard; results depend on your session stickiness and prompt reuse. We'll instrument the cache hit-rate in the run.
04:04 Jordan: On sizing we often map token throughput to GPU capacity via tokens/sec and model variant. We'll deliver a recommendation: hosted for pilot, then sizing for Dedicated if you need predictable tail latency at scale.
04:20 Marcus: We have a budget constraint — ideally cost should be <= 35% of current OpenAI spend but with better p99.
04:29 Jordan: We'll model unit economics in the benchmark plan.
04:33 Priya: A few clarifying Qs: typical sequence lengths distribution, percent of streaming vs non-streaming calls, and whether you do beam search or sampling.
04:44 Lena: Mostly sampling/top-p, and we stream token-by-token for the interactive flow. The service also has a batch generation path for nightly catalog generation (longer outputs).
04:57 Priya: Streaming affects tail-latency measurement — we measure e2e first-byte latency and time-to-last-token as two metrics.
05:08 Marcus: Could you also surface cold-start wall times if an idle model needs to spin up? We see some cold starts when traffic drops overnight.
05:16 Priya: Yes, we'll include startup latency and model load times in the heatmap, annotated by time-of-day.
05:23 Jordan: On timelines — suggested: we get logs by Feb 18, Redwood shares the benchmark plan by Feb 16, baseline run tentatively Feb 22 (one day), then stress/soak Feb 24-25, and a results review on Feb 28. Does that align?
05:40 Lena: That works, we'd like an executive one-pager with recommended Dedicated capacity if needed.
05:47 Jordan: We'll include a capacity recommendation and break down unit costs.
05:51 Sofia: On security, we need to confirm whether you support customer-managed KMS and provide audit trails per request.
05:58 Jordan: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS via AWS KMS/HSM — we'll send the integration checklist.
06:06 Priya: Quick note on data handling during the pilot: logs used for replay are ephemeral and we can run in a sandbox VPC if you want network isolation.
06:16 Sofia: Sandbox VPC is required for us for production-adjacent tests.
06:20 Jordan: Noted. We'll provision a VPC sandbox for the run.
06:25 Marcus: For the traffic replay — can you accept synthetic arrival curves? We might want you to scale bursts beyond our real data to find failure points.
06:33 Priya: Absolutely, we'll replay recorded traces and then apply scaling factors and shorter inter-arrival jitter to simulate tight bursts.
06:42 Lena: One more thing — quality regression tolerance. We don't want to see >2% drop in top-k accuracy for recommendations after changing model or quantization.
06:54 Priya: We'll run a set of prompts (eval set) and compute metric deltas; if quality drops are beyond threshold we'll flag. Please provide an eval prompt-set.
07:05 Jordan: Ok, to summarize success criteria that we'll include in the SOW:
07:10 Jordan: 1) P95 < 250ms and P99 < 600ms under your observed baseline QPS envelope; 2) sustained throughput capacity estimate (tokens/sec and max concurrent sessions) for 95/99 operating points; 3) cost per 1M tokens estimate; 4) evidence of cache hit-rate improvement and cold start durations; 5) no more than 2% quality regression on agreed eval prompts.
07:37 Marcus: Sounds good. What about post-POC handoff — do you provide runbooks for Dedicated?
07:43 Priya: Yes we'll include runbook, autoscaling policy recommendations, and rollback playbook.
07:49 Lena: Any blockers on our side besides log export and eval set?
07:53 Sofia: I'll need the security checklist; also need contract redlines from legal but that's separate.
07:59 Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 and the checklist in the follow-up email.
08:03 Marcus: Great. One logistical Q — which models will you run in the baseline? Our current is gpt-like open model.
08:12 Priya: We'll match the model family you currently use (you said open-model gpt-like). For cost modeling we'll also run a 4-bit quantized variant to show unit savings and impact to latency.
08:24 Lena: Ok. Also interested in seeing a heatmap visualization — QPS vs time with annotations for tail events and cold-starts.
08:32 Priya: We'll generate that in the report, plus concurrency histograms and token percentile tables.
08:38 Jordan: Alright let's capture actions and dates — Marcus will upload logs by 2027-02-18, Lena will share eval set, Sofia will confirm KMS/residency requirements, Jordan will send SOW and pricing by 2027-02-16, Priya will prepare harness by 2027-02-20.
08:56 Lena: Any competitor comparisons you plan to show?
08:59 Jordan: We'll show a high-level comparison (OpenAI current spend vs Redwood projected vs self-host Triton costs) — not a deep bench.
09:08 Sofia: Fine.
09:10 Jordan: Ok final check — everyone comfortable with Feb 22 baseline run?
09:14 Lena: Yes.
09:15 Marcus: Yes.
09:16 Sofia: Yes.
09:17 Jordan: Great — thanks all. We'll send the follow-up with links and SOW.
09:22 (call ends)
